name: Damakawa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Sole description McGill 2008, The Damakawa language (SOAS, 6 pp.) read in full via Internet Archive copy of cicipu.org/papers/: wordlist survey report, contains no stress/tone/prosody statement

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart. 2008. The Damakawa language. Ms, School of Oriental and African Studies, London, 28 April 2008. 6 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Read in full (Internet Archive copy of cicipu.org/papers/). Field-visit report with an untonemarked wordlist (~45 numbered items + ~30 other words + ~20 phrases) elicited from rememberers; sections: Language situation, Interviews, Wordlist, Other words, Some phrases, Relationship with other West Kainji languages. No sentence mentions stress, tone, accent, pitch, prosody or syllables.
Cites only the ISO change request and McGill 2008; states ~80 words and phrases were collected with difficulty in April 2008. Nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. Comparative Kainji: Main text ('Kainji language overview'). Circulation draft, 11 May 2012. 369 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 3.8.5 Damakawa (pp. 30-31) reproduces McGill 2008's sociolinguistic paragraph and Photo 5 'The last rememberers of Damakawa', adding 'The data, which is included in the comparative wordlist, is too fragmentary to be certain of the affiliation of Damakawa.' In the Phonology chapter, 4.8.5 'Damakawa ?' (p. 36) is an empty heading with no text; Damakawa is labelled 'Unknown'/'?' in the comparative-wordlist headers. No statement on stress or tone for Damakawa (tone sections exist only for Cinda and Hungwəryə).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, edition III (circulation draft, 3 Dec 2012). Entry 78 'Damakawa'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Entry 78 (text p. ~1723 of extraction) gives names, location, population, classification ('Benue-Congo: Kainji: Western Kainji: Kambari cluster', reliability caveat), 'Source: McGill (2008)'. Nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart John. 2009. Gender and person agreement in Cicipu discourse. PhD dissertation, SOAS, University of London. 483 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Grammar of Cicipu, not Damakawa. Damakawa occurs only as 'Damakawa [?]' in a West Kainji classification tree and in the bibliography entry for McGill 2008. Nothing on Damakawa prosody.

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart. 2009. The genetic classification of Cicipu. Ms, SOAS, 6 May 2009. 16 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Cicipu classification paper; no mention of Damakawa at all.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2008. Change Request 2008-041: create [dam] Damakawa (submitted by Stuart McGill; adopted 2009-01-16). SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Administrative form; states that 'The only source of information on the Damakawa is an unpublished report that I have compiled' (McGill 2008) and that the data is 'a list of eighty words together with some phrases'. Nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart. 2012. The Kainji languages. Ms, SOAS, London, 30 August 2012. 7 pp. (Glottolog ref 306337)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Short family overview; may repeat the classification remark on Damakawa. No reason to expect a prosody statement for a language known only from an 80-word rememberer list.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. n.d. The West Kainji Languages of Northwestern Nigeria. Unpublished manuscript, 243 pp. (Glottolog ref 66310)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only Glottolog-listed West Kainji overview not opened; almost certainly a comparative wordlist compilation that, if it includes Damakawa at all, would carry McGill's untonemarked forms. Very unlikely to state anything about stress; listed for completeness. Superseded by Blench & McGill 2012 Comparative Kainji draft, which was read and is silent.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page dama1268 and reference records 66310 (Blench n.d., The West Kainji Languages of Northwestern Nigeria, 243 pp. ms), 115581 (McGill 2009), 306337 (McGill 2012, The Kainji languages, 7 pp. ms)
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Glottolog 5.3 lists three refs for Damakawa; none is coded as a grammar, phonology or sketch of Damakawa (language code fields name other Kainji languages). Blench n.d. and McGill 2012 were not located online (Blench's live site is behind a captcha by automated download; cicipu.org is dead).
